note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Fever and systemic illness for ~7 days. Recent travel to Vietnam; returned 4 weeks ago with rural exposure (trekking, cycling through farmland).
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Fever ~7 days with intermittent hot sweats and chills; generalized myalgia, nausea, poor oral intake, fatigue. Night sweats and feeling hot/sweaty during day; also feeling cold at times. Paracetamol and ibuprofen taken (OTC) with minimal symptomatic relief.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: denied.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: denied.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: denied.
  - Drooling: denied.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: hay fever (pollen allergy) only; no acute nasal/ocular complaints reported.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: denied.
  - Dyspnea: denied.
  - Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): no swelling reported.
  - Ear/neck symptoms: no ear pain; no neck stiffness.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior similar febrile episodes documented.
  - Chronic back pain under physiotherapy; exercises for posture/strengthening.
  - No hospitalizations or adrenaline/epinephrine injections mentioned.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: pollen (hay fever). No drug allergies reported.
  - Current medications: Seroxat — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Short-term/OTC medications: paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented; ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Malaria prophylaxis taken while in Vietnam — patient cannot recall name; reports it was likely a daily regimen and that she took “another one on top of the first one” (name and exact regimen not documented; uncertainty/conflict noted).
- Relevant social/context:
  - Works as a nurse; reports being significantly symptomatic and feels unable to work until evaluated.
  - Agreed to attend central London clinic today; advised option to attend local A&E if more convenient.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: no swelling reported or observed in transcript.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: no stridor or noisy breathing reported; no dyspnea reported.
- Mental status and associated features: patient appears systemically unwell — tired, sweaty, nauseous; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not recorded.

Assessment:
- Clinical impression:
  - Acute febrile illness of 7 days with systemic features (fever, night sweats, myalgia, nausea) and recent travel to rural areas in Vietnam — travel-associated infection (including malaria) is a key consideration.
  - No focal ENT source identified on history (no sore throat, ear symptoms, upper airway compromise, or swelling).
- Key justifications from transcript:
  - Persistent fever and night sweats for ~7 days despite OTC antipyretics.
  - Recent travel to malaria-endemic area with rural exposure returned 4 weeks ago.
  - No reported ENT signs/symptoms to suggest primary throat or otic source.
- Conflict noted:
  - Malaria prophylaxis details uncertain: patient stated it was likely daily and also said she took “another one on top of the first one” — exact regimen/name not provided.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Arrange face-to-face clinical examination in central London clinic today.
  - Request blood tests after clinical assessment, including thick and thin blood films for malaria and inflammatory markers (and other routine bloods as indicated by clinician).
  - Advised patient not to attend work until evaluation and tests are completed.
  - If unable/unwilling to attend clinic, advised option to attend local A&E with written note in consultation for reception.
- Specific instructions to patient:
  - Patient to attend the clinic appointment; doctor will send a message to admin to book.
  - Patient instructed to ring the number left in the consultation notes after a few minutes so admin can slot her in (exact phone number documented in consultation notes — patient to use that).
- Escalation criteria / red flags instructed:
  - Seek urgent care (attend A&E) for any breathing difficulty, voice change, sensation of throat closing, or worsening/swelling of face/lips/tongue/uvula.
- Follow-up:
  - Clinical review in clinic after examination and blood tests; clinician to determine urgency of testing and further management based on findings.
  - If clinic unavailable, take the written note to local A&E for same blood tests (including malaria films).
- Additional items discussed:
  - Doctor will document recommended tests and rationale in consultation notes for presentation to clinic/A&E.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No recorded vital signs (temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, SpO2).
  - No physical examination findings documented (including airway exam, throat exam, lung auscultation).
  - No laboratory results (pending tests).
  - Malaria prophylaxis drug name and dosing not provided.
  - Seroxat dose/route/frequency not provided.
  - Specific inflammatory markers/tests beyond “inflammatory markers” not detailed.
  - No documented plan for empirical therapy pending results, if applicable.
  - No record of prior anaphylaxis plan or auto-injector (not expected here but relevant for ENT/allergy checklist).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Unclear details about malaria prophylaxis: patient uncertain of exact medication; stated both “daily” and “another one on top of the first one” — uncertainty/conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall clear and intelligible. Minor brief inaudible/repeated phrases but sufficient for clinical documentation.
